temperatureRange.notes: Source-specific 1987 liquid/FCC assessment in its original pure-liquid reference convention, not SGTE canonical unary integration. Recommended high-temperature use 1238.15-2100 K: lower bound follows source discussion above 965 C; upper bound is an intentional teaching window, not a published validity limit. Low-temperature ordered/intermediate phases and gas excluded. One FCC function represents both solid solutions. R=8.314 J/(mol K) is an explicitly chosen rounded reference constant; its precision is not specified in Table 5.

unaryEndpointProvenance.notes: Table 5 supplies the complete original FCC-minus-liquid functions, with both pure-liquid functions zero. Owner authorized preserving this assessment after the SGTE compatibility audit. Not absolute SER Gibbs energies; do not combine with canonical unary endpoint phases.

binaryInteractionProvenance.notes: Table 5 polynomial in xPt converted algebraically, without fitting, to RK powers of xAg-xPt. Solid S_ex=-10.6 xAg xPt J/(mol K).

references.citation: I. Karakaya and W. T. Thompson, The Ag-Pt (Silver-Platinum) System, Bulletin of Alloy Phase Diagrams 8 (1987) 334-340; Table 5 p.337 and Table 6 p.340.

ownerValidation.cttObservation: Owner visually confirmed FCC miscibility gap near xPt 0.36-0.825 at 1238.15 K and peritectic Ag-rich contact near 0.405 at 1459.15 K (corrected typo). Visual Pt melting estimate 2046.15 K is approximate; Ag melting is below the supplied window and was not measured.
ownerValidation.scope: Quantitative owner-reader agreement and qualitative owner CTT confirmation; not precise melting-point validation.

verification.validationNotes: Original 1987 liquid/FCC equations, not SGTE unary integration. Temperature window 1238.15-2100 K. Table 6 mismatch up to 0.00291044 mole fraction Pt is retained; no coefficient fitting. See validation-diagnostics.json and source-audit.md.
